ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The paired words 'kill' (殺) and 'keep alive or give life' (活): killing and giving life.
EvidenceBody: It appears with other paired Linji-house terms in the list 'killing and giving life, granting and taking, provisional and actual, illuminating and functioning' (殺活縱奪、權實照用). Fixed forms include 'free in killing and giving life' (殺活自在, 51 occurrences), 'killing or giving life according to the occasion' (殺活臨時), and 'killing and giving life at the same time or at different times' (殺活同時／殺活不同時). The record explicitly pairs it with the sword that kills a person (殺人刀) and the sword that gives a person life (活人劍): one turning word is the killing sword, one the life-giving sword, one kills and gives life at once, and one does so at different times (一轉語是殺人刀、一轉語是活人劍、一轉語殺活同時、一轉語殺活不同時). Another passage asks directly, 'What is killing?' (敢問如何是殺), and records Shiqi Tongyun responding by raising a foot. The headword occurs 1,275 times in 280 allowlisted texts, overwhelmingly in expositions and formula lists in later recorded sayings and lamp records. Juelang Daosheng also pairs unfettered killing and giving life with displaying a formal public scene, preserving the same two-way authority rather than introducing another sense.
